# X6 R43 — Releasable shared-target resource: exact BRC serial histories and two-step residual memory

Date: 2026-11-20 (Asia/Shanghai). Research context: \`RS-X6-NATIVE-TIME-DYNAMICS\`.
Status: \`CONDITIONAL_AUTHOR_PROOF / EXACT_FINITE_ENUMERATION_PASS / NOT_INDEPENDENTLY_REVIEWED\`.
This is an independent portable scientific return, not a current TASK CLAIM, native PROGRESS, Result or Review.

## Frozen source, preserved lineage and model type

Scientific P000 input is \`awdawmip/enterprise-math@a72226e2430ffa4786321ac86e7f0c599d5f0389:p000_reality_foundation.json\` (frozen P000 V5), together with the same pin's \`definitions/P000_DISCRETE_DIRECTION_TRIADIC_BALANCE_20260905.md\` and \`definitions/ENTERPRISE_JOINT_RELATION_OBSERVER_PRESERVATION_20260905.json\`. Spatial Cell addresses use the native affine \`Z^6\` torsor, with a chosen anchor rather than a global origin. This extends the R42 static Port-sensitive shared-target model (\`research_notes/portable_direct/2026-11-20_x6_r42_port_sensitive_resource_graph.md\`, Git blob \`ba93c9d60ff4250190631987b339c851d91aac11\`) and the R41 conflict-graph/clock work. No physical successor law for \`TRIADIC_CLOSURE_E\` is inferred from this candidate.

Two individually named sources A and B each carry one indivisible, ordered, nonzero three-force frame. Each source may transfer its **whole frame** at most once, using one of p named eligible Port alternatives A0,...,A(p-1) or B0,...,B(p-1). Port 0 of both sources targets the same Cell c; all other candidate targets are mutually distinct. Here p=3 is the native three-Port candidate of R42; p=1,2 are restrictions of available ports, **not** one- or two-force primitive balances. p>3 is a mathematical stress-test extension, not an additional native primitive Port claim.

Add one public, separately typed resource-service event R, allowed precisely when c is occupied. R empties c; it does **not** reset an already fired source. A Port-0 transfer is allowed only if its source is unused and c is empty. Other Port transfers require only an unused source. Thus source consumption is permanent, but Port-0 resource exclusion is temporary and may reverse following R. R is a control/resource event, not an independently admitted three-force balance.

A complete decorated state is \`(a,b,o)\`, where \`a,b in {-1,0,...,p-1}\` record each source's chosen Port (-1=unused), and \`o in {-1,A,B}\` identifies the current occupant of c (-1=empty). Start at \`(-1,-1,-1)\`. The successful event alphabet keeps all source and Port names, plus R. Every event word is its own positive integer BRC serial history (coefficient 1); path count means the number of successful named serial words, never a signed amplitude.

## Theorem R43.1 — Exact finite serial counts for every p>=1

The number of successful prefix words of event length h=0,1,2,3,4 is exactly

\[
\boxed{(W_0,W_1,W_2,W_3,W_4)=(1,\,2p,\,2p^2,\,6p-4,\,2),\qquad W_h=0\ (h>4).}
\]

Consequently the total number of successful named serial histories, including the empty one, is \`2p^2+8p-1\`. The complete decorated reachable-state count is \`(p+1)(p+3)\`.

**Proof of word counts.** The first event chooses any of 2p source Ports. Two-event words consist of two source events, in either order, with all p^2 Port pairs except the two orders of the shared Port-0/Port-0 conflict, giving \`2(p^2-1)\`; or one Port-0 event followed by R, giving two more. Hence \`W_2=2p^2\`. A three-event word has either a Port-0 event, then R, then any of the p Ports of the other source (2p choices); or two source events, exactly one of which uses Port 0, followed by R (four choices of source order and which source uses Port 0, times p-1 nonshared choices). Thus \`W_3=2p+4(p-1)=6p-4\`. The only four-event words are \`A0 R B0 R\` and \`B0 R A0 R\`. No longer word exists: at most two source events and each R empties the target filled by a previous Port-0 action.

**Proof of reachable-state count.** Initially there is one state. Exactly one used source gives \`2(p+1)\` states: p-1 nonshared Port choices with c empty, or Port 0 before/after its release. Both sources used give \`(p-1)^2+4(p-1)+3\` states: neither uses Port 0, exactly one uses Port 0 (with its occupied/released alternatives), or both use Port 0 (two possible final occupants plus the cleared state). Their sum is \`(p+1)(p+3)\`. Every enumerated state has a successful word witness, and the three categories are disjoint.

For p=3, the resulting \`W=(1,6,18,14,2)\` gives **41** histories and **24** decorated states. In contrast the static one-shared-cross-edge R42 graph has 23 histories. Release adds 18 legal words without changing the two source triads or the chosen X6 shared-target geometry.

## Theorem R43.2 — Seven exact future-language classes and a two-step mask counterexample

Two decorated states are equivalent exactly when they permit the same complete future **named successful-event language**. For every p>=1, the reachable states collapse to exactly **seven** future-language classes. They are:

1. U: both sources unused, target empty.
2. A-occupied: A used, B unused, target occupied.
3. A-clear: A used, B unused, target empty.
4. B-occupied: B used, A unused, target occupied.
5. B-clear: B used, A unused, target empty.
6. T-occupied: both sources used, target occupied.
7. T-clear: both sources used, target empty.

Each class has a deterministic transition law depending only on its class and the named event, so it is a future-language congruence. The seven classes have pairwise distinct languages.

**Sharper enabled-mask criterion.** For p>=2, the seven classes have seven different sets of immediately enabled event labels. Thus the current enabled mask alone is a complete future-language Markov coordinate. For p=1, there are only five distinct enabled masks, although still seven future-language classes: A-occupied, B-occupied and T-occupied all enable precisely \`{R}\`. Their distinct future behavior becomes visible after release. In particular let

- \`s=A0\` (A fired, B available, c occupied);
- \`t=A0 R B0\` (both fired, c occupied).

Both states currently enable exactly \`{R}\`. The two-event suffix \`R B0\` is legal from s but illegal from t, and no one-event suffix distinguishes them. Therefore one-step enabled-mask equality is **not** sufficient for full future-language equivalence when p=1. The three different \`{R}\` futures require a three-valued residual mode (two binary bits if encoded uniformly inside that mask fiber).

**Proof.** When both sources are unused, all A and B Port labels are enabled. When exactly A has fired, its Port identity no longer affects the future except through the current occupancy bit: B may use its p Ports if c is empty, or only its p-1 nonshared Ports plus R if c is occupied. The symmetric statement holds with A/B interchanged. Once both have fired, only R may remain, depending on occupancy. These seven descriptions are closed under every legal successor. For p>=2 their enabled sets are pairwise distinct: U enables both source families; the A-only and B-only cases have different source labels; occupancy adds R and removes the remaining Port-0 label; T-occupied enables R alone; T-clear has no enabled label. For p=1, the three R-only classes are distinguished after R by the respective successor enabled sets \`{B0}\`, \`{A0}\`, and the empty set; all other class pairs are already distinguished in one event. Hence exactly seven classes in every case.

The quotient has a three-bit minimum fixed-length state index (\`ceil(log2 7)=3\`) for the declared future named-word observer. The full current source/Port/occupancy observer still requires \`ceil(log2((p+1)(p+3)))\` bits. Event length is an ordered event counter, not a proven physical heartbeat duration.

## Precise relationship to R42 and native P000

R42's static independence polynomial works only when a fired action permanently disables the actions it conflicts with. The release event R re-enables the previously forbidden other-source Port 0, so the static deletion law \`E -> E \ N[a]\` is false for this dynamic system. The finite seven-class quotient above supplies an exact update-closed repair. For the actual R42 three-Port shared-target geometry, the enabled mask remains sufficient under this particular release rule; reduced Port visibility can expose an additional two-step residual. The underlying three-force frame is never broken by a transfer.

The physical bridge remains an open dependency: a native X6 Cell/Link/Port service law must specify whether target release is actually admissible, its source/provenance trace, and its clock; only then can this conditional automaton be compared with real \`TRIADIC_CLOSURE_E\` dynamics. No theorem here asserts a measured physical 3-bit minimum.

## Exact executable evidence and continuation

Self-contained verifier: \`research_notes/portable_direct/x6_r43_releasable_shared_target_verify.py\`.
Results: \`research_notes/portable_direct/x6_r43_releasable_shared_target_results.json\`.

It builds the complete reachable transition graph for p=1,...,6, enumerates every successful named event word (maximum four events), independently checks the closed counts and state formula, refines future-language equivalence to its fixed point, and checks all ordered state pairs plus the shortest \`R B0\` witness at p=1. The finite test covers **all legal states and words** in those six models; general p formulas and seven-class classification follow from the proofs above. No outside scientific literature is claimed as novel.

Next discriminating unit: allow source re-enabling or an identity-dependent release/rotation response, then test whether two full three-Port states can share the same immediate enabled mask but differ in their future languages. Such a witness would identify which new native Link/Port/source residual a real transition law must preserve. Preserve R41/R42 provenance and the present author-side, unreviewed scope.
